findings.description: SHEET-MARK-002 states the conversion is `round_half_to_even(price × 100)`. The real `price_to_cents` deliberately does NOT do this: it scales to micro-cents (`const SCALE: i128 = 1_000_000`), then folds via a local `round_half_up` helper (div_euclid/rem_euclid) that rounds a half-cent tie UP, never to-even — the function's own doc comment says this is 'cheaper than `pt_core::round_half_to_even` at this call site.' Tests pin the opposite-of-spec behavior exactly: `price_to_cents(1.005) == Cents(101)` and `price_to_cents(1.015) == Cents(102)` (both round up); true round-half-to-even would send 100.5 → 100 (nearest even), not 101. A1/A2/A3 (reading the EARS literally) all implemented some form of round-half-to-even (via `f64::round_ties_even` or a hand-rolled even-check) — none produced the real code's half-up tie-break. B1/B2/B3 (reconstructing from code+tests only) unanimously wrote the rule as half-up-never-to-even with the exact `1.005→101`/`1.015→102` pins, directly contradicting the EARS text they never saw. Even the crate's own top-of-file doc comment (lib.rs line 17: 'The price→Cents conversion uses pt_core::round_half_to_even, the project's single canonical rounding site') is stale/wrong about this same function.

SHEET-MARK-002's anomaly clause is scoped narrowly to 'a positive price that rounds to 0 Cents.' It says nothing about a price that IS exactly 0.0 or negative. The real code's guard is `if cents <= 0 { return Err(SubCent) }`, which fires for ANY non-positive folded result — tests pin `price_to_cents(0.0) == Err(SubCent)` and `price_to_cents(-5.0) == Err(SubCent)`, not just a positive sub-cent price rounding down. All three A outputs, reading the EARS narrowly, treat exact `price == 0.0` as a legitimate `Ok(Cents(0))` mark (A1 assumption #6, A2 assumption #4, A3 assumption #3) — a clean 3/3 A-direction miss driven by the EARS's narrow wording, contradicted by the real code/tests. All three B outputs correctly captured the broader 'any ≤0 folded result → SubCent' rule with matching pinned examples.

Within the A direction itself, negative-price and non-finite-price handling were NOT unanimous, and where they disagreed, the majority reading diverged from real code. A1 does not special-case NaN/negative at all (relies on Rust's saturating float→int cast, so a NaN price would fall through to `Ok(Cents(0))` since `price > 0.0` is false for NaN) and A2 likewise passes a negative price through arithmetically with no anomaly — both contradict the real code, which returns `Err(Permanent)` for NaN and `Err(SubCent)` for any negative price. Only A3 added an explicit negative-price anomaly branch (coincidentally matching the real degrade-not-negative-mark outcome, albeit under an invented `Negative` reason rather than `SubCent`).

Non-finite input handling (NaN/±Infinity) is entirely unaddressed by the EARS text but is a pinned, tested code behavior: `price_to_cents(f64::NAN)` and `price_to_cents(f64::INFINITY)` both return `Err(DegradeReason::Permanent)` — a reason distinct from the `SubCent` anomaly the EARS discusses, and also triggered if the intermediate scaled value itself overflows to non-finite. All three B outputs surfaced this uniformly as a `Permanent` variant separate from `SubCent`; SHEET-MARK-002 never mentions non-finite prices.

The EARS phrase 'round_half_to_even(price × 100)' reads as a single float-rounding operation. The real code never rounds a raw float directly to a cent: it scales to a ×1,000,000 integer numerator (`SCALE: i128 = 1_000_000`), rounds that once, then folds to whole cents via integer `div_euclid`/`rem_euclid` — explicitly so 'the scaled-integer decision — not the float's own rounding — decides the cent' (per the function's doc comment). All three B outputs pinned the exact `SCALE = 1_000_000` constant and described this two-step scale-then-fold mechanism identically; none of the three A outputs (reasonably, given the EARS's literal phrasing) invented this intermediate scaling — all did a single rounding step at ×100.
